text:
Maria: rolling out rwd-13b-quant changes now (prefetch/kernel policy tweak). Deploying to prod.

deploy-bot: rollout completed for canary group -> 2026-03-17T22:01Z :white_check_mark:

Maria: looking at nocturnal traffic, token/sec for rwd-13b-quant dropped ~35% since deploy, p95 latency +120ms, error rate unchanged. graphs: https://grafana.redwood/exp/rwd-13b-quant

Kevin: link?

Maria: https://grafana.redwood/d/rwd-13b-quant/ctb-throughput?orgId=1

Ash: I repro on staging with same flags. Kernel selector seems to prefer 'matmul-streamed' -> then falls back to 'matmul-fallback' for longer seqlens because of new cost heuristic. That fallback path does an extra memcpy and bypasses fast KV prefetch, so CTB waits longer for KV warmup.

Ash: repro logs:
```
[2026-03-17T21:58:05Z] kernel_policy: choose matmul-streamed for batch=32 seqlen=512
[2026-03-17T21:58:05Z] kernel_policy: fallback to matmul-fallback due to mem_est>threshold
[2026-03-17T21:58:05Z] kv_cache: miss_rate increased, prefetch deferred
```

Lucy: which PR changed the heuristic? I recall PR #4512 touched kernel cost heuristics.

Kevin: starting bisect on main against last known good (2026-03-16). `git bisect start --term-good main@{2026-03-16} --term-bad main`

Kevin: bisect landed on commit abcdef123456 (PR #4512) — kernel estimation tweak: reduced mem_threshold by 20%.

Kevin: perf numbers (staging): before commit token/sec ~ 220k, after commit ~145k for same traffic mix.

Dave: can we revert and hold? This is a rollout blocker for rwd-13b-quant.

Maria: reverting now.

Maria: `git revert abcdef123456 -m 1` -> opened revert PR #4520

deploy-bot: revert PR #4520 merged and deployed to prod (canary -> 2026-03-17T22:45Z)

sre-bot: alert auto-resolved: ctb-tokensec-drop for rwd-13b-quant

Lucy: nice. Followups: add a regression perf test to CI that runs a miniature CTB harness and measures token/sec with representative seqlen distribution. Also add a safety gate: if kernel selection decision increases memcpy bytes beyond X% in canary, fail rollout.

Ash: filing issues: #perf-ci-harness and #kernel-metrics-gate

Maria: action items: (1) revert PR in prod (done), (2) add CI perf test (Ash), (3) restore kernel threshold but add unit tests to cost estimator (Kevin), (4) add alert that triggers on sustained token/sec drop >20% (SRE)

Kevin: I'll send a small patch that keeps thresholds but prefers stable path for CTB until we validate with perf harness.

Dave: thanks everyone. reassigning to eng-runtime perf board. :thumbsup:
